_about: Rick's 24 Shorts, per-video values of each film-level camera number (tools/measure/film_motion.py instrument; source episodes/card-maker-ban/analysis/data/motion.json, 2026-11-09). check_film.py reads pass/warn from 'gate'; the distribution is here so the bands can be re-cut without re-measuring.

pct_settled.text: camera at rest (< 2 px/f), % of frames

holds_10s.fix: too few: break long travels with a resting station; too many: station hopping, merge stations and let one move flow through them

travel_p90.target: 2.1-6.3 (Rick median 3.0; Railroads and Roller Coasters 4.7). CB 2026-11-10: the scene decides, but some moves must flow
travel_p90.fix: under 2.1: every move is a short hop, let one or two moves follow something through the set for 4-5 s; over 6.3: insert a rest inside the longest moves

p50.fix: too high: slow down, rest more; too low: add creep to the rests

cuts_10s.fix: merge takes; cut only on place or time jumps

settled_at_longword.text: camera at rest on long words, %
settled_at_longword.fix: word stations need a rest that starts 0-6 f before the word

words_per_s.fix: voice too slow or too fast: regenerate at the right pace, never time-stretch

pct_hold03.text: camera dead still (< 0.3 px/f), % of frames
pct_hold03.fix: the rests are parked: raise the creep on those stations or add a drift (film_plan.py REST_PX)

_about_2026_11_10: CB 2026-11-10 after the comparison with five of Rick's films (references/remeasure/compare_2026-11-10): travel_p90 and holds_10s became two-sided bands. Camera movement depends on the scene (CB), so out-of-band values warn before they fail.
